column1: # Character roster for the Claude Code roleplay bookends.
# Format:  UNIVERSE | Character Name | emoji | traits | signature line (optional)
# Delimiter is "|" (not tab, despite the filename's history) and surrounding
# whitespace is trimmed, so columns can be padded for readability. Lines
# starting with "#" and lines with fewer than 4 fields are skipped.
# Selection is TWO-STAGE: bin/roleplay-roll picks a UNIVERSE, then a character
# within it. That is deliberate. A flat roll across every row lets the biggest
# groups take most of the rolls. Two-stage holds each universe at its own share
# no matter how lopsided the groups get, so you can add 40 more tarot cards
# without burying the Techpriest.
# The cost of that choice: per-character odds are NOT equal across universes.
# A universe with few members over-represents each of them.
# WEIGHTS tilt both stages. Each is a share relative to its peers: everything
# weighs 1 by default, 2 is twice as likely as a peer at 1, 0.5 is half as likely,
# and 0 means it never rolls. The rows stay in the file, so 0 is a reversible way
# to bench something.
#   @universe  | NAME | weight    share among the universes
#   @character | NAME | weight    share among the members of that character's universe
# Names must match exactly. `roleplay-roll --check` prints the resulting odds for
# every character and reports any weight line that matches nothing.
# SIGNATURE LINE (5th field, optional): a character's one overwhelmingly famous
# quote. Each roll decides whether it is unlocked or spent, at ROLEPLAY_CATCHPHRASE
# odds (default 1/3), and the injected tag says which. Name the quote here rather
# than banning it -- an unconditional ban was the previous design and it was too
# blunt. The problem was never the quote, only that it appeared every single time.
# Leave the field off entirely for characters with no such line (most of them).
# EXAMPLES: examples.md (next to this file) has four worked bookends for every
# character here, plus a fifth for the seven with a signature line showing it
# used on the roll where it is unlocked. Nothing reads it at runtime -- it is a
# style reference for when a universe starts sounding samey.
# Weights. Anything not listed weighs 1.
@universe | FAVORITES | 3
@universe | TAROT     | 0.5
@universe | ZODIAC    | 0.25
@universe | THE LEGEND OF ZELDA | 2
@universe | STEEL MAGNOLIAS     | 2
